Subject: Exec sync: OKR commitments & QBR slate

Team — attaching the draft QBR slate and a proposed OKR roster for the quarter. High level ask: please confirm owner commitments and any blockers by EOD Thursday (2027-09-23).

Context: we want a tight QBR narrative that ties product launches + Dedicated capacity SLAs to customer outcomes and top-line bookings. The attached slate (QBR_Slate_Q4_2027_v1.pdf) includes the story arc and a 12-slide appendix for metrics. The roster (OKR_Owners_Roster_v2.xlsx) maps owners to key results and supporting experiments.

Immediate asks:
- Owners: confirm "yes" / "needs discussion" / "no" next to each OKR row in the roster.
- Risks: flag any capacity/org dependency that prevents hitting the key result.
- Data: if you need runs/queries, call out specific dashboards (I can loop infra).

I expect we’ll lock owners here and run a short dry-run on Thurs 9/23 at 3pm PT (calendar link below). If Acme wants a pre-read call, Lina — happy to sync.

Attachments: QBR_Slate_Q4_2027_v1.pdf (slide deck), OKR_Owners_Roster_v2.xlsx (owners matrix)

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Strategy & Operations
Redwood Inference

- For the QBR narrative, add a single customer vignette (Acme) on slide 4 showing before/after latency and cost impact. Lina — can you share a short metric we can cite? Even a 2–3 bullet quote is helpful.

I can confirm owners on KR2 and KR4. For KR3 (throughput improvements) we need a resource callout — we may need to request a 6-week engineers-of-focus commitment from infra to meet the timeline.

- Average inference latency pre-integration: ~280ms; post: ~95ms (95th percentile).

Also, a short pre-QBR call would be useful to make sure the wording is appropriate for our legal/comms teams. I’m available Thu 9/23 11:00–11:30 PT if that works.
